title: Proper Venting in Drainage Systems
description: An effective drainage system relies on much more than gravity and downward-sloping pipes; it requires a properly balanced venting network. Without adequate air intake from plumbing vent stacks, the rush of falling wastewater creates negative pressure that can siphon water straight out of fixture traps. When trap seals are compromised, sewer gases enter the living space unhindered, creating health hazards and unpleasant odors. Professional drainage design ensures every fixture is adequately vented to maintain atmospheric pressure and keep waste moving smoothly.
